title: 7 Levels of AI Game Dev: From One Prompt to 200,000 Sales
author: Comet7777
selftext:
I spend way too much time scrolling AI game posts here and on X, and I started noticing they could all be put into certain buckets. So I ranked them, based off of the "7 level of rappers" trend I've seen online (though I first saw this with soccer players!).

\*Disclaimer - this is for **fun**, not super serious besides wanting our community to do better than posting one-prompt lazy posting\*

**Level 1: The AI toy.** A cool animation or a single mechanic. Impressive in 10 seconds, but there’s no game yet. Or really, even gameplay. I've posted tons of these myself once I discovered PixelLab lol. Learning how to make the most of this level can get you towards level 5 if handled with care and intention. These posts can also be educational for other creators to understand tools and techniques. The reason it's level 1 is that more often than not it's a "look what I made with AI in 5 seconds! Game dev is DEAD" bullshit post (notice their character animation has 6 fingers? lol).

**Level 2: The one-prompt game.** “I typed one sentence and got this.” Playable, but it’s mostly the model doing the work. No semblance of an actual full game. Usually these "games" taper off beyond quick social media experiments because actually iterating on a game correctly requires way more planning than anything a single prompt generation can do. 

**Level 3: The frontier one-shot.** Someone tests a new model and it builds something legitimately impressive in one go. Better than level 2, but again, this makes an impressive demo/prototype - likely can't complete a full gameplay loop yet. Same as level 2 though, I've yet to really see games like these start iterating meaningfully - but that could change. 

**Level 4: The mashup.** A known IP plus a known genre (Diablo Survivors, Pokemon Survivors Dragon Ball "temple run" type of game). These get a shit ton of clicks due to the power of the IP and the nuance take of a blend of genres. And because you're mashing stuff up, often times there's already good gameplay loops inherent in these projects - but you can't make any money off of it, so often times these projects get stale due to the price someone is paying to keep enhancing them. Also, if you're messing with Nintendo, the cease and desist letter is always chasing you like the monster from "It Follows". 

**Level 5: Build in public.** An original game idea with a real art direction, posting progress every week and building an audience. A history of progress being made, especially with addressing feedback from a community. Not only is there progress, but there's multiple iterations of gameplay already established - just likely lacks polish and scale. 

**Level 6: The demo.** A real Steam page with a free demo that strangers play and an actual wishlist. The game has matured enough to make it on to a Steam page (different bar to pass than itch.io). Presenting a demo then allows for better feedback and a growing wishlist. It's a baseball player who has gotten to 3rd base - almost there. 

**Level 7: Shipped and selling.** An AI game that has gone through the previous levels and has not only been released, but has actually found commercial success. Slotbound is the example everyone knows: 200K+ copies in one week + an pattern and history of the game going through the various levels before it.

comments.author: Kojinto
comments.body: Cool video! It's kinda neat to know I am somewhere in between level 5 and 6 with my personal project. A shared-world single-player online RPG that has 10s of thousands of simulated NPCs with LLM-powered dialogue, procedural quests, and flow-state-inducing (up to) 4v4 action combat where a really strong final hit can send an enemy flying a mile into the distance or more, and they'll remember you and come and find you if they survive.

comments.author: LiquidZebra
comments.body:
“This is the gold standard for what an ai game should be”. For a pixel art auto battler? On Steam, a platform with a trillion impressions? 

I think Slotbound is a flappy bird level fluke, with shady Chinese wishlists and purchases.
